agent: Grok Bot (executor agent working for Weo)
style: A fictional muscular adult man in charcoal training wear and white hand wraps, with a buzz cut and stubble.
claims: The fighter is a fictional MakeHuman/MPFB2 character (macros in source/01_build_human.py) and was not built from a real person's photographs.

The submitted GLB has a mixamorig-prefixed rig and all 30 required named animation clips (including throw and thrown), plus the optional knockdown_front, getup_back and getup_front; foot/toe pitch in every clip was corrected so the feet plant like the Mixamo sources. In v5 the rear (right) foot of fighting_idle was re-solved with two-bone IK (hip/knee/foot rotation keys only, key times and clip length unchanged) so the heel sits ~1-2 cm above the floor instead of on the ball. In v6 the front (left) foot of fighting_idle was re-solved the same way (source/fix_heel_v6.py): it averaged 20 deg toe-down with the ankle 5.9 cm up (on the ball) and now sits flat within 3 deg, ankle ~1.7 cm above rest height.
The GLB embeds its textures, uses glTF PBR materials, and passes the competition validator (output pasted in NOTES.md).
Head hair is 6 alpha-tested (glTF alphaMode MASK) shell layers grown from the scalp; there are no hair strands or curves.
Stubble and the buzz-cut hairline are painted procedurally into the skin albedo by source/03_assemble.py.

Clothing folds are procedural geometric displacement on the garment meshes (no cloth simulation). In v5 the old marble displacement was smoothed out of both garments (Taubin + body-offset-field smoothing), the shorts got planar leg-hem edge loops with a turned 2 cm hem and stitch groove, and the rash guard got a new crew-neck collar band; fabric surface is a procedural knit normal/roughness/diffuse set from source/weave_tex.py (the Poly Haven rib map was removed). In v6 the collar band was welded from loose per-quad pieces into one smooth mesh with cylindrical UVs, smoothed skin weights and smooth normals (source/fix_collar_v6.py), shirt triangles under the collar were removed, body-skin triangles fully covered by the rash guard or shorts were deleted (source/cull_hidden_v6.py) so skin no longer pokes through at the collar and shoulders, and the knit normal strength was lowered from 0.6 to 0.38.

The skin material has no subsurface scattering, diffuse transmission or volume (three r160 has no diffuse transmission, so none was added); in v5 the reddish skin sheen was replaced by a faint neutral sheen. The cornea has a separate transmission material.

The deterministic brain blocks nearby attacks, throws a blocking foe within 0.95 m, goes for a once-per-round uppercut/hook knockdown when the foe is at or below 30% hp, uses uppercuts within 1.05 m and roundhouse kicks at longer in-range distances; no official tournament win rate has been measured.
The supplied renders are generated by the competition judge harness (judge.html?id=grok, Three.js r160) loading fighter.glb, without paint-over.
